rows.Incident Description: -Informed by Mass/Liza at 0230hrs, Mr. Chen (registrant of room#2191) claimed that his money was missing from room.
rows.Subject: Missing cash in room
rows.Investigation/Follow Up 1: Missing cash/ valuable items in hotel
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
-Front Office/Angus,  Security/Oscar and Housekeeping/Vincent attended to room and met up with Mr. Chen. 
-Mr. Chen claimed that he had one thousand to two thousand United States Dollar (USD $1, 000-$2, 000),  three thousand to ten thousand Ren Min Bi (RMB$3, 000-$10, 000) and one thousand Malaysian Ringgit (MYR $1, 000) which were all kept at his two separate envelope like bags and kept at the bottom of his backpack. The backpack was left on the chair near the writing desk.
-Mr. Chen claimed that he had checked that the money was still inside his backpack after entering the room at 1150hrs on 31Dec.
-Mr. Chen claimed that the location of the envelopes was different from when he left the room and the envelopes were all empty after returning to room at 0224hrs on 01 January 2026.
- Moreover,  Mr. Chen also mentioned that he had taken the flight from Cambodia to Macau in the morning.
-Mr. Chen stated that he stays alone and did not give the room keys to any third party. 
-Front Office/Angus offered internal investigation which Mr. Chen accepted.

According to Visionline:
-Mr. Chen entered room at 1150hrs and left room at 1203hrs on 31 December 2025.
-Housekeeping team entered room at 1824hrs on 31 December 2025.
-In Room Dining team entered room 1831hrs on 31 December 2025.
-Housekeeping team entered room at 2042hrs on 31 December 2025.
-Mr. Chen returned to room at 0224hrs on 01 January 2026

-Mass/Liza was duly informed.
-Risk Management was informed via E-mail.
-For more detail,  please refer to Security Log#DL20260000108.

Updated by TX - A shift on 01Jan
- As CI need times to investigate the case thus Mass Marketing/ Lisa was informed that we will update her once the investigation result come out from CI.

rows.Incident Description: Informed by Security Team at 2047hrs, Mr. He (registrant of room 628) dispute with F&B colleague at Casino Pit 25 Casino Service Bar.
rows.Subject: Guest dispute with F&B colleague
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
-Mr. He approached Casino Service Bar and placed a hot milk tea on the food display glass cabinet.
-Food and Beverage colleague (English speaker) informed Mr. He several times that it was not allowed to place the hot drinks there due to safety reason,  but Mr. He had no response.
-The F&B colleague then moved his hot mike tea to the marble table next to Mr. He.
-When Mr. He noticed that his glass had been moved to the marble table,  he pointed his cane at the colleague and shouted at her. 
-After Mr. He left the sence,  F&B colleague informed the Security team for assistance.
-Mr. He was found by Security inside casino. According to Mr. He,  he did not understand what the F&B colleague said due to language barrier. He temporary put the hot milk tea on the food cabinet as he needed to present his Wynn Membership Card for food redemption. 
-Later,  the F&B colleague found a crack in the glass on the counter and suspected that Mr. He had caused it.
-After Surveillance footage review,  it was confirmed that Mr. He was not responsible for the cracked glass.
-Mass Marketing/Flash and Casino Service Bar/Nelson were duly informed.

rows.Incident Description: - Informed by Security Team at 0345hrs, Mr. Liu (registrant of room #719) took away total three thousand and four hundred Wynn casino chips (HKD$3,400, 3 x $1000 & and 4 x $100) which should belong to hotel at Pit 24 Table 6.
rows.Subject: Security Assistance
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
According to Security Team:
- In the first round,  Mr. Liu and a casino guest (no information could be obtained) both bet on “Banker”. 
- Mr. Liu bet one thousand and four hundred chips (HKD$1, 400),  and the casino guest bet one thousand chips (HKD$1, 000). 
- The result showed “Player” won but Mr. Liu took away his one thousand and four hundred losing chips (HKD$1, 400). The casino guest left the scene immediately after lost the game,  his one thousand losing chips (HKD$1, 000) was still on the table. 
- At that time,  the dealer forgot to collect back the casino guest’s one thousand losing chips (HKD$1, 000).
- In the second round,  the result showed “Banker” won. However,  due to the dealer’s mistake in first round,  the casino guest’s one thousand chips (HKD$1, 000) increased to two thousand chips (HKD$2, 000). Mr. Liu claimed the two thousand chips (HKD$2, 000) belong to him.

- Security Team escorted Mr. Liu to interview room and asked Mr. Liu to return total three thousand and four hundred Wynn casino chips (HKD$3, 400) to hotel. However,  Mr. Liu only accepted to return two thousand chips (HKD$2,  000) to hotel which agreed by Gaming Team.
- Security Team decided to ban Mr. Liu from entering property for one month. Room #719 will be checked out today.
- For more information,  please refer to the Security Log #DL20260030640.

-According to Mr. Yang,  all lights suddenly went off in room 812 three times tonight. 
At 2330hrs,  all lights suddenly went off while his wife taking a bath at bathroom then Mr. Yang pressed the control panel to turn on the lights. 
At 0010hrs,  all lights suddenly went off again while Guest Room Attendant assisting to fix the speaker in bedroom as Mr. Yang found the speaker automatically shut down after powering on at noon. Then the Guest Room Attendant informed Facilities teams to fix the light issue. The Facilities teams suspected that there was a problem with the sensor system,  so they shut it down.
The speaker was unable to be fixed and did not have a new one to replace at that time by housekeeping team. Mr. Yang agreed to replace a new speaker on next day.
At 0100hrs the light issue happened again,  while Mr. Yang going to the bathroom,  so he called Guest Service Centre to raise a comment..
-Front Office/Jenny extended apology and offered room move,  however Mr. Yang turned down room move as his wife and son were going to sleep but agreed Facilities team to fix the issue.
-Facilities team was informed to fix the issue again and completed at 0130hrs.
-Mr. Yang claimed other electrical infrastructure functioning normally.
-The facilities team suspected that the wiring for the lights loosening,  caused all lights suddenly went off and he has fixed it.
-Two Adults and one children's breakfast at Lakeside Trattoria on this visit,  complimentary room upgrade to one bedroom suite on next visits were offered to Mr. Yang as recovery which Mr. Yang accepted.
-Housekeeping/Ivy was duly informed.

rows.Incident Description:
- Informed by Spa Department at 2039hrs, Ms. Zhang (wife of registrant Mr. Liu from room #1307) requested Security assistance as she stated that she lost her gold bracelet at the Wynn Spa.

Information of Ms. Zhang:
- Name: Zhang, Hong
- Date of birth: 21-June-1970
- Hong Kong ID card number: R616568(A)
- Wynn membership card number: 51834507
rows.Subject: Guest Assistance
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
-According to footage review,  confirmed that Ms. Zhang arrived at Wynn Spa reception at 1413hrs. She was wearing the gold bracelet on her right hand and also had other jewelry on both hands at that time.
- Ms. Zhang claimed that before she entered the Spa treatment room “Lavender”,  she took off all her jewelry and put it into the inner layer of her handbag,  then locked it in the female changing room locker number 21. The locker uses an electronic lock with a self-set password,  but Ms. Zhang claimed there was a Spa colleague watching her to set the password.
- According to the footage review,  confirmed that there was nothing that wearing on her hands when Ms. Zhang left the Wynn Spa at 1709hrs and went back to room #1307.
- At 2000hrs,  Ms. Zhang stated that when she wanted to wear all her jewelry kept in her handbag and left the room for dinner,  she found that one of the jewelries (gold bracelet) was missing,  so she reported it to Spa Department.
- After Spa colleagues checked all the lockers in the female changing room,  no gold bracelet was found.
- Security/Oscar and Front Office/Candice attended to room to inform Ms. Zhang of the above result. Ms. Zhang agreed to pass the case to Cooperate Investigation Department for internal investigation first.
- Mass Marketing/Flash and registrant Mr. Liu’s marketing Host/Jermond were informed.
- For more details,  please refer to the Security Log #DL20260050730.

Updated by BH - C shift on 22,  February 2026:
- Received call from Security Team/Suman at 0647hrs,  after footage review by Security Team again,  confirmed that Ms. Zhang did not wear the gold bracelet but wear other jewelries bracelet on both hands while she left the property at 1236hrs. At 1410hrs,  Ms. Zhang came back to the property via Wynn Club Entrance,  she was holding her phone in her right hand with an orange color phone strap hanging from it. At 1413hrs,  Ms. Zhang arrived at Wynn Spa reception.
- Next shift Duty Manager will inform Ms. Zhang for the above result.

Updated by CC - B shift on 23,  February 2026:
- Security/Oscar,  Marketing Host/Jermond and Front Office/Candice attended to room at 2014hrs to update Ms. Zhang the above result.
- Ms. Zhang did not accept the result and claimed that she must lock the gold bracelet in the female changing room locker.
- Ms. Zhang decided to file the case to police. Security/Oscar escorted police officer to room for investigation.
- After mediation by police officer and Security,  Ms. Zhang changed her mind to pass to Cooperate Investigation Department for handling at this moment.
- Next shift Duty Manager will continue to follow up once received any update from Security Team.

Updated by CC - B shift on 24,  February 2026:
- According to Security/Oscar,  no suspicion was found after Cooperate Investigation Department investigation.
- Marketing Host/Jermond informed registrant Mr. Liu the above result,  and Mr. Liu did not pursue the case further at this moment.
- Mass Marketing On-duty Manager/Man was informed.

rows.Incident Description: -Informed by Guest Services Center Team at 0840hrs, Ms. Zhang (Registrant of Room #1408) reported that she found five thousand Hong Kong Dollar (HKD $5,000) was missing from room after she woke up.
rows.Subject: Missing cash in room
rows.Investigation/Follow Up 1: Missing cash/ valuable items in hotel
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
-Front Office/Angus and Security/Kelvin attended to room to show concern.
-Ms. Zhang claimed that she cashed out twenty thousand seven hundred Hong Kong Dollar (HKD $20, 700) at West Cage (near Cigar Emporium) around 0300hrs on 16 March 2026 and took five thousand Hong Kong Dollar (HKD $5, 000) to gamble at the casino.
-Ms. Zhang then returned to room at 0416hrs to rest and kept fifteen thousand seven hundred Hong Kong Dollar (HKD $15, 700) inside her backpack.
-Ms. Zhang claimed that when she woke up to check on the cash,  she found that there was only ten thousand seven hundred Hong Kong Dollar (HKD $10, 700) left.
-According to Visionline,  there was no open and close door record after 0416hrs which was when Ms. Zhang returned to room with the cash.
-Front Office/Angus offered to room search but was turned down by Ms. Zhang.
-Footage review showed that Ms. Zhang approached West Cage at 0345hrs to cashout,  however,  the amount that Ms. Zhang cashed out was fifteen thousand seven hundred Hong Kong Dollar (HKD $15, 700) which does not match with the amount mentioned by Ms. Zhang.
-Ms. Zhang was informed the result,  but she did not accept.
-Ms. Zhang stated that she counted the money before heading to cash out and she remember clearly that the amount was twenty thousand seven hundred Hong Kong Dollar (HKD$20, 700).
-Surveillance team assisted to check footage again and found at 0342hrs,  Ms. Zhang gave some Wynn Casino chips (unable to identify the amount) to a male casino patron (no information could be obtained). 
-Ms. Zhang was informed the result and claimed that she remembers now.
-Ms. Zhang claimed that she gave ten thousand Hong Kong Dollar Wynn Casino chip (HKD $10, 000x1) to her husband (no information could be obtained) at the beginning and gave an extra five thousand Hong Kong Dollar Wynn Casino chip (HKD $5, 000x1) to her husband afterwards.
-Ms. Zhang thanked hotel for the assistance and did not pursue any further.
-Housekeeping/Rita and Telemarketing/Catherine was duly informed.
-For more detail,  please refer to security log#DL20260070703.

- Front Office/Angus,  Housekeeping/Maggie and Security/Daniel attended to room to show concern.

- Ms. Li claimed that she was in the room when Housekeeping Team threw the rubbish,  but she was sleeping and was not paying attention.
- Ms. Li claimed that she did not leave the room for the whole day on 28th March 2026.
- Ms. Li only realized the necklace was missing around 2320hrs when she was looking for it.
- Front Office/Angus offered room search and the result turned out as negative.
- Front Office/Angus offered to pass the case to internal investigation which was accepted by Ms. Li.
- Housekeeping/Maggie confirmed that all the rubbish from room#1237 was disposed.
- Housekeeping/Maggie will assist to confirm with the according housekeeping team member on 29th March 2026.
- According to Visionline,  Housekeeping Team entered room at 1654hrs for throwing out the rubbish and left the room at 1657hrs.
- Mass Marketing/Flash was duly informed.
- Risk Management was informed via email.

Updated by CC - A Shift on 29Mar:

- Security/Gary and Mass Marketing/Jill were informed.
- Risk Management will be informed via email.

-Ms. Li's phone number: 0086 131 6823 7710.
-Risk Management was informed via email.

rows.Incident Description:
At 0000hrs on 01Jan, DM was informed by the Room Controller that Mr. Au, occupying due-out Room #608, refused to check out and vacate the room.
DM contacted Mr. Au, who expressed strong dissatisfaction and stated that his host had promised to reserve the room until 03 Jan. DM explained that the original reservation was scheduled to check out on 31 Dec and that no extension was possible due to full occupancy. Mr. Au did not accept this explanation and declined further communication.

DM consulted with Mass ODM and confirmed that the Mass Marketing Team could cover the late check-out penalty but could not extend the booking. Mass/Erwin advised that FO should proceed with standard procedure and involve the Security Team if necessary. At 0200hrs, DM proceeded to the room with Security SM for further handling.

Upon arrival, Mr. Au contacted his host and reiterated dissatisfaction, stating that the host had promised an extension until 03 Jan. The host confirmed that no room block was available due to high occupancy. Mr. Au refused to check out and requested police involvement if forced to vacate. After further discussion with Mass ODM, DM offered to extend Mr. Au’s stay for one additional night. DM presented the registration card and clearly informed Mr. Au that the check-out date would be 01 Jan. Mr. Au acknowledged and signed the registration card without further pursuit.
rows.Subject: Guest Dispute on Reservation Stay Period
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Investigation:
Membership Tier of the registered guest Mr. Au: Gold Card.

-Room #608,  C#4945927,  reserved on 30Dec for a one-night stay and check out on 31Dec
-Mr. Au checked in on 30 Dec,  registration card indicated check-out on 31 Dec and was signed by the guest
-Room #608 remained due out on 31Dec. FO conducted departure audits at 1444hrs,  1654hrs,  and 2220hrs and found unpacked luggage in the room
-GRM informed host for follow-up. Host/Yoppy confirmed intent to extend but was awaiting room block
-At 1958hrs,  Mr. Au approached FO for a room key. FOSA noted due-out status with comment that Host intent to extend. FOSA advised guest to contact host.
-At 2327hrs,  Mr. Au again requested a room key. FOSA reiterated due-out status and advised check-out if extension was not confirmed. Mr. Au acknowledged and requested key to retrieve luggage
-At 2346hrs,  Room Controller confirmed guest remained in the room and contacted Mr. Au,  who refused to leave. The case was escalated to DM.

Follow Up:
-Mass ODM was informed.
-DM please take note

rows.Incident Description:
At 1525hrs, DM/Chris Chan was notified by the GSC that Mr. Chan, the registered guest of Room #2711, had requested ambulance assistance due to his 3-year-old boy had sustained an injury.

DM together with the Security Team, attended to the room immediately. Upon arrival, DM found the child was accompanied by Mr. Chan, and a non-registered guest - Ms. Tsui. They claimed to be the parent of the child. Upon assessment, the child was found conscious and sustained an injury to his left forehead, with bleeding observed, resulting in 1.5 cm wound. According to Mr. Chan, while the child was playing on the floor, he accidentally fell and struck his head against the left side lower of the bed frame. First-aid treatment was administered on-site, including the application of bandages. After First-aid treatment, the wound stopped bleeding. 

DM expressed concern for his condition and advised guest to visit hospital for medical treatment, which Mr. Chan accepted. An ambulance was promptly summoned and arrived at the Staff Entrance. The child was transported to the Staff Entrance using their own baby stroller, assisted by the Security Team. Subsequently, the child was accompanied by Mr. Chan and Ms. Tsui and was transferred to Macau Kiang Wu Hospital for further medical assessment as per guests' request.

DM business card was provided to guests and were advised to contact DM should they require any further assistance. Guests thanked for the assistance without further pursuit.

CCTV footage identified the caller as the guest from Room #1342. The DM placed a courtesy call to Mr. Huang, the registrant of room #1342 and confirmed he was the reporting guest. An apology was extended, and a fruit amenity was arranged as a gesture of hotel courtesy.

At 2225hrs, TP-6 returned to normal operation. The investigation concluded that the incident was caused by a faulty retardation control component, which has since been replaced. Total stopped: 2hrs 34mins.

rows.Incident Description:
At 0230hrs, DM/Bill was notified by Marketing Host/George that Mr. Guo, the registrant of Room #1856, reported an alleged missing cash incident related to his stay in Room #1662 from 01–03 January 2026.

The Security team was informed and accompanied the DM to meet with Mr. Guo and his two non-inhouse companions in Room #1856. Mr. Guo reported an alleged loss of MYR 3,000 (approximately MOP 5,940) from his sling bag. He stated that the cash was placed in his bag and the last seen prior to his check‑in on 01 January, and that the bag had remained inside the room throughout his stay. He only discovered the cash missing after moving to his new room, #1856, on 03 January.

The DM explained that there were no staff entry records for Room #1856 after Mr. Guo’s check‑in, which led him to believe that the incident must have occurred in his previous room, #1662. During the enquiry, Mr. Guo mentioned that some of his friends had visited him while he was inside the room; however, he stated that he trusted them. He therefore requested a review of CCTV footage and an investigation into the housekeeping staff members who had accessed Room #1662 during his stay.

After discussion, Mr. Guo opted not to file a police report and preferred that the hotel handle the matter internally. He was informed that an internal investigation had been initiated and that its findings would be shared with him within 2–3 weeks.

rows.Incident Description:
At 2000hrs, DM/Karen was informed by Bell Captain/Dennis that an ambulance had arrived at the North Entrance and Security was at the scene. DM proceeded to the scene immediately. Upon enquiry, a non-registered guest, Mr. Gao, from checked out Room #1813, reported outside PSP on his own. Mr. Gao stated that he left the room at around 1500hrs alone, while his girlfriend remained in the room. Later, he was unable to re-enter as the room keys were not working, and he could not contact his girlfriend. Concerned for her well-being, he requested police assistance, claiming that his girlfriend was feeling unwell inside the room and he was worried about her.

CCTV footage revealed that Mr. Gao left the room at 1539hrs, with further footage still under review. Security OM/Philip, DM/Karen, and PSP went up to the room for inspection and found the female guest (Mr. Gao’s girlfriend) sleeping safely inside the room. Security escorted Mr. Gao to the room. After DM and Security’s explanation, Mr. Gao and his girlfriend cancelled the ambulance assistance and agreed to vacate the room after packing their belongings without further pursuit. 

As per Security’s instruction, no further action will be taken against the registrant.

At approximately 0745 hrs, the DM/Mena was informed by the Security Supervisor and FOSA/ Eric that a non-in-house guest, Mr. Bai, requested to speak with the Duty Manager to express dissatisfaction regarding the attitude and case handling by the Security Team.

DM met Mr. Bai at the North VIP Registration area and learned that he reported a missing casino chip valued at $2,000 from a gaming table. According to Mr. Bai, the table dealer escalated the matter only after his third report that the chip was suspected to have been taken by someone.

However, after approximately 20 minutes of CCTV review, it was determined that the suspect had already left the property and no identifying information was available. Mr. Bai was informed that recovery would only be possible if the suspect returned and was apprehended by Security.

Mr. Bai expressed frustration, believing that Security’s inefficiency allowed the suspect to escape and that he was misled into thinking the chip could be retrieved. He also reported that the Security officer displayed poor attitude when advising him to report the case to the police if he did not wish the hotel to handle it further. Mr. Bai later decided not to pursue the matter with the police after learning that doing so might require him to attend court proceedings.

DM acknowledged Mr. Bai’s concerns, extended apologies for the negative experience, and assured him that his feedback would be escalated to the relevant department management for review. Mr. Bai was advised to contact the Duty Manager should he require further assistance.

rows.Incident Description:
-At 0020hrs, DM/Bill was informed by the Housekeeping (HSKP) team that a non-registered couple in Room #2211 reported finding an unknown Rolex watch on the bedside table and requested its removal. 

-DM/Bill and Security SM/Ego attended the room and identified the non-registered couple as Mr. Li and Ms. Guo. Mr. Li stated the room was arranged by his friend Mr. Huang – the room registrant. 

A thorough review was conducted involving GSC, HSKP GRA, door access records, and the Security team. The timeline is as follows:
•	1747 hrs: Mr. Huang checked in at North Reception and was issued room keys #243118 and #243119 for Room #2211.
•	1747–1929 hrs: Mr. Huang accessed the room using the issued keys.
•	2120–2249 hrs: An unidentified couple accessed the room using the same keys.
•	2250 hrs: A male guest called GSC from Room #2211 requesting cleaning and bedding change.
•	2329 hrs: HSKP attended the room. The bed and amenities had been used, and the room appeared messy with no luggage present. During bedding change, GRA discovered a Rolex watch on the bed. With DM approval, the watch was placed on the bedside table.
•	0015 hrs on 15 Jan: Mr. Li and Ms. Guo entered the room and reported the Rolex watch to GRA.

Mr. Li was advised to confirm with Mr. Huang for the ownership of the watch. Furthermore, Security explained to Mr. Li and Ms. Guo regarding the hotel policy, they agreed to leave the room without further issue. In addition, Security and FODM decided to keep the watch inside the room. Room keys were overridden asp Security due to suspected room selling. 

Subsequently, DM received a call from Host/Jason, who stated that Mr. Huang claimed ownership of the watch and requested it be handed to the host for safekeeping. DM and Security declined this request and advised Mr. Huang to return to the hotel personally for verification due to the high-value nature of the item. Host then contacted Mr. Huang and he claimed will return to the hotel shortly.

rows.Incident Description:
At 1905hrs, DM/Karen was informed by GSC that Ms. Jiao, the registered sharer of room #2655, had called and requested to speak with the Manager on Duty, without initially disclosing the reason. The call was transferred to the DM.

Ms. Jiao stated that earlier she had approached FOSA/Carol at the North Main Reception to request luggage delivery to the room, while all other counters and staff were occupied assisting guests. When she arrived at the counter, FOSA/Carol asked her to wait for a moment as she was assisting another guest. Subsequently, FOSA/Carol assisted a lady who was standing behind her. Ms. Jiao questioned why the service was not handled on a first-come, first-served basis, as she believed she had arrived first. FOSA/Carol explained that the lady had arrived earlier but had briefly stepped away to retrieve her visa slip from her luggage for check-in registration and had returned shortly thereafter. Ms. Jiao then waited to the side.

However, after FOSA/Carol completed the registration for the lady, she ignored her and proceeded to assist another male guest. Ms. Jiao felt this constituted double standards in service. As a result, she called to lodge a complaint against FOSA/Carol, citing service quality issues and perceived unfair treatment at the North Main Reception. DM/Karen extended sincere apologies to Ms. Jiao for the unpleasant experience and assured her that the incident would be thoroughly investigated. Ms. Jiao requested a formal follow-up reply after the investigation, as she felt the incident had negatively affected her hotel experience.

Following the investigation, DM/Karen met Ms. Jiao in her room and apologized that the experience did not meet the high standards the hotel strives to uphold. As a service recovery gesture, DM offered fruit and chocolate amenities, which Ms. Jiao declined. She instead requested a personal apology from FOSA/Carol. DM politely declined this request but assured internal coaching and disciplinary review would be conducted. As alternative, DM offered a MOP $1,000 F&B credit, which Ms. Jiao eventually accepted without further pursuit.
rows.Subject: Guest Complaint - Service Quality
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Investigation:
-Membership tier of the registrant - Mr. Fu: Chairman Card.
-Membership tier of the registered sharer - Ms. Jiao: Red Card.

According to FOSA/Carol:
Carol reported that she was assisting Ms. Hu with the check‑in process when Ms. Hu briefly stepped away to retrieve her visa slip. During this moment,  Ms. Jiao approached the counter requesting luggage delivery. Carol asked her to wait and explained that she would complete the ongoing check‑in first. This prompted Ms. Jiao to question the service sequence and raise her voice. She became confrontational,  asked for Carol’s name,  and began taking photos despite being advised not to.

To prevent further escalation,  Carol minimized verbal interaction and focused on completing Ms. Hu’s check‑in. Noticing that another team member was available,  she attempted to direct Ms. Jiao to the available counter for assistance. However,  Ms. Jiao declined and insisted on waiting for Carol. Once Ms. Hu’s check‑in was completed,  Carol invited Ms. Jiao to step forward so she could assist her. Ms. Jiao refused and instead repeated her request to have four pieces of luggage delivered separately to four rooms,  though she could not recall the room numbers for three of the rooms. She stated she would inform Carol once she remembered.

During this time,  a male guest approached and handed over a key card insert for key issuance. As Ms. Jiao still could not provide the room numbers required for her request,  Carol proceeded to assist the male guest. She acknowledged that accepting the key card insert while still interacting with Ms. Jiao was inconsistent with service standards.

CCTV Review Findings:
•  18:42:45 – Ms. Hu approached FOSA/Carol and presented her membership card and ID for check-in. 
•  18:43:05 – Ms. Hu stepped away to retrieve her visa slip from her luggage at the North Main Reception entrance while FOSA/Carol continued scanning the ID. 
•  18:43:12 – Ms. Jiao entered the North Main Reception. 
•  18:43:16 – Ms. Jiao approached FOSA/Carol’s counter,  which was vacant at the time,  while the other three counters were occupied. Simultaneously,  Ms. Hu returned to the same counter. FOSA/Carol interacted briefly with Ms. Jiao and then continued the check-in process for Ms. Hu. Ms. Jiao then moved a bit to beside. 
•  18:44:47 – FOSA/Carol informed Ms. Jiao that counter #03 was available and gestured for her to proceed to that counter. 
•  18:45:14 – Ms. Jiao took out her phone and began taking photos of Carol’s name tag. 
•  18:46:27 – FOSA/Carol completed the registration process for Ms. Hu,  who then left the counter. 
•  18:46:28 – FOSA/Carol began assisting Ms. Jiao. Since Ms. Jiao was standing to the side,  another male guest approached directly in front of the counter and handed over a key card insert. Carol assisted the male guest with key issuance.
•  18:47:15 – Ms. Jiao moved to the adjacent counter and requested assistance from SFOSA/Sonia. 
•  18:51:50 – Ms. Jiao left the North Main Reception and proceeded to the casino.

Follow Up:
-Mass ODM was informed.
-Coaching would be issued to FOSA/Carol. 
-DM please take note.

rows.Incident Item Name: Delay Pick Up or Drop Off - WMP
rows.Incident Description: Wilson Ning called at 09:08 and couldn’t find his limo at Nova Grand BOC. Dispatch called limo driver Chio In at 09:08, driver stated that he was waiting at Nova Grand instead of Nova Grand Bank of China. The driver took 3 minutes to arrive at Nova Grand BOC, Wilson Ning got into the limo at 09:11 and arrived WC at 09:23, which was 8 mins late from limo reservation time.
rows.Subject: Delay Pick Up and Drop Off - Executive Wilson Ning
rows.Investigation/Follow Up 1: Delay Pick Up or Drop Off - WMP
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Investigation 

Driver Chio In overlooked the booking from UCS and waited for Wilson Ning at Nova Grand. During their conversation,  Wilson mentioned he almost took a taxi because he couldn’t see the limo. The driver extended his apologies for the service delay.  

Chio In explained that the order message has confused him because it showed Nova Grand at the first pick up and Nova grand BOC at the second line.  Leading driver thought Nova Grand was the pick up location.

Follow up action

Informed Eliza about the incident and extended apologies. Also let her know that the Nova Grand Bank of China code has been added to the system. Will brief our drivers to read the instructions carefully in order to provide accurate limo services.

Brief all dispatchers to remark all booking location in chinese when confirming TBC booking and make clear instruction when dispatch job to drivers.

rows.Incident Description:
At 1846hrs, Limo Manager/Herminio received a report from Hotel Limousine Driver/Jacky Kei regarding a
traffic incident involving his arranged hotel limousine MZ-8392 and motorcycle MW9664. The collision
occurred at approximately 1846hrs at the TIS roundabout driveway. No passengers were present in either
vehicle, and no injuries were reported.
According to Limo Driver Jacky Kei, he had just completed a drop off for Executive Ms. Zoe Zou and was
returning to the hotel when the incident occurred. While traveling through the TIS roundabout, a
motorcycle attempted to overtake the limousine from the right rear side. Due to insufficient space, the
motorcycle rider’s left foot made contact with the right-side rear bumper of the limousine.
Limo/Jacky immediately notified the Limousine Office and contacted the traffic police. Limo AM/Charlie
attended the scene to document and assist with the situation. Police officer #26224 arrived, conducted
an inspection, and concluded that neither party was at fault, as no visible damage was found on either
vehicle.
rows.Subject: Traffic Collision
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Investigation:
-The motorcycle rider declined to provide personal information after the police determined that no party
was at fault.
-The Fleet Specialist inspected limousine MZ 8392 and confirmed that no damage was observed.
Follow Up:
-FO DM was notified.
-Security Team was informed.
-Risk Management was informed.
-Limo Driver Jacky Kei has been reminded and coached to consistently maintain a professional driving
attitude and adhere to safe driving practices at all times.

rows.Incident Description:
-At 1800hrs, DM/Bill was informed by BDV/Nino that Mr. Liang, a non-registered guest of Room #1317, requested to speak with the Duty Manager regarding a complaint about the attitude of the Skycab Ambassador at the Resort Station. DM met Mr. Liang at the North VIP Reception, where he identified himself as the husband of the room registrant, Ms. Zhou. 

Mr. Liang reported that he had taken his 1-year-old child for a Skycab ride at around 1711hrs. After completing one round and returning to the Resort Station, his child wished to take another trip. Observing that the priority line was empty, Mr. Liang asked the Skycab Ambassador/Charlotte, if they could remain in the cabin for one more round. Where, Charlotte insisted that they must alight from the cabin and rejoin the queue, explaining that there were many non–in-house guests waiting. During this interaction, Mr. Liang stated that his child became frightened by Charlotte’s tone and demeanor. Ultimately, they exited the cabin and boarded another one immediately afterward.

Mr. Liang expressed dissatisfaction with the experience, questioning:
1.	Why in-house hotel guests were not given priority over non–in-house guests, particularly considering he was traveling with a young child.
2.	Why they were required to leave the cabin when the priority line was empty, only to board another cabin immediately afterward. He believed the requirement to alight was unnecessary and felt that Charlotte’s actions were intentionally targeted at him.

DM conveyed understanding and extended sincere apologies for the unpleasant experience, further assured Mr. Liang that the issue would be personally reviewed with Charlotte and that appropriate coaching and training would be provided to prevent recurrence. As a gesture of courtesy, fruit and chocolate amenities, along with a Wynn bear, were arranged and delivered to Mr. Liang. Mr. Liang accepted and did not pursue further.
rows.Subject: Guest Complaint - Staff Attitude
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Investigation:
-Both Mr. Liang and Ms. Zhou did not have membership.

-CCTV footage from the Resort Station was reviewed,  and the following timeline was established:
•	1711hrs – Mr. Liang and his child entered the priority line at the Resort Station and boarded Cabin #16.
•	1723hrs – Cabin #16 returned to the Resort Station. After a brief interaction with Skycab Ambassador/Charlotte,  Mr. Liang and his child alighted from Cabin #16.
•	There were around 90 guests queuing in the general line at Resort Station general line while no guest queuing in the priority line.
•	1724hrs – Mr. Liang and his child proceeded to board Cabin #18.
•	1736hrs – Upon returning to the Resort Station,  they exited Cabin #18. Mr. Liang approached Skycab Ambassador/Yuki and requested to raise a complaint with the Manager. BDV/Nino was notified. 
•	1737hrs – Mr. Liang and his child then boarded Cabin #21.
•	1749hrs – After completing the ride,  Mr. Liang and his child returned to the Resort Station and met by Nino. Mr. Liang was escorted to the South VIP Reception and DM/Bill was notified.

rows.Incident Description:
At 1300hrs, DM/Mena was notified by the Security Team that the registrant of Room #0741, Ms. Zhao, approached the Casino Cage requesting assistance regarding a missing slot ticket.

Upon inquiry, Ms. Zhao stated that she printed a slot ticket in the amount of HKS $10,020 during the morning of 25 January and subsequently left the casino. She only became aware that the ticket was missing on the morning of 26 January.

She then exited the casino without dropping any personal belongings. Subsequently, on 26 January 2026 at approximately 1010 hours, an unidentified female suspect approached the one of slot machines and inserted a ticket with unknown amount of money for play. The suspect later printed a slot ticket totaling HKD 11,000, which included the victim’s remaining balance. The suspect proceeded to cash out the ticket at Main Cage Window #08 and thereafter departed the property via the hotel shuttle bus. Based on the above findings, it is suspected that Ms. Zhao accidentally dropped the slot ticket, which was later picked up and used by the unidentified suspect as per Security Team.

Ms. Zhao was informed the findings, she opted not to report the case to the police and passed the case to hotel to handle the case internally. As per Security Management Team, the unidentified female suspect has been placed on the Security Watchlist for further monitoring.

rows.Incident Description:
At 1109hrs, DM/Mena was notified by the Shuttle Bus Team of a traffic collision involving the WP Hotel Shuttle Bus (MY-6492) and a City of Dreams (COD) Shuttle Bus (AC-4394). The incident occurred at approximately 1105hrs at the Shuttle Bus Station of Macau International Airport. At the time of the incident, two female passengers were on board the WP Hotel Shuttle Bus. No injuries were reported.

According to the Shuttle Bus Team, the WP Hotel Shuttle Bus was stationary at the designated parking area of the shuttle bus station for guest loading from Macau International Airport to Wynn Palace. At that time, the COD Shuttle Bus driver attempted to reverse but failed to properly observe the surrounding road conditions, resulting in the COD Shuttle Bus’s right front colliding with the left front of the WP Hotel Shuttle Bus. Consequently, the WP Hotel Shuttle Bus sustained damage to its left-front passenger door with the door glass cracked, along with damage to the left-side mirror.

The shuttle bus driver immediately reported the incident to the Shuttle Bus Manager and contacted the Traffic Police. A replacement WP shuttle bus (MX-6624) was promptly dispatched and successfully transferred the guests from Macau International Airport to the hotel without further delay.

Following police assessment, the COD Shuttle Bus driver was determined to be at fault. As both shuttle buses are operated by the same vendor company, the vendor will internally handle and settle the repair costs. The incident has been escalated to Risk Management for reference and record.

DM subsequently met with the involved passengers, Ms. Tsang and Ms. Djauw, at the East Shuttle Bus Station to express concern and provide assistance. It was confirmed that they were visiting Wynn Palace for shopping purposes and were not in-house guests. Both passengers confirmed that no injuries were sustained and that no further assistance was required.

rows.Incident Description:
At 2212hrs, DM/Chris Chan was reported by FOSA/Mandy that Ms. Zhao, the registered sharer of room #2091, had requested medical assistance for her 4-year-old son, who had sustained an injury at the North Suite Floor lift lobby.

The Security Team was notified and accompanied the DM to meet Ms. Zhao, the injured child, and five companions (two females, three girls). All guests were then escorted to the North VIP Registration DM Room for further handling. Ms. Zhao reported that the injury occurred while they were waiting for the lift at the Ground Floor lobby. The child had placed his hand on the lift door, and his fingers became caught in the gap as the door opened. She immediately pulled his hand free and subsequently discovered that he had injured the index and middle fingers of his right hand.

Upon the assessment, DM observed swelling and redness, along with a 1 cm superficial abrasion, with no active bleeding. First aid was administered by Security Team, including the application of an ice pack. Shortly after, Mr. Kong (the registrant of room #2091, child's father) arrived. DM recommended that the child be taken to the hospital for further evaluation, and Mr. Kong agreed. 

A hotel limousine was arranged immediately. The child, accompanied by Mr. Kong and Ms. Zhao, was escorted by DM to the vehicle and transported to Macau CHCSJ Hospital, accompanied by FOS/Ida. Guests expressed appreciation and raised no further concerns at that time.

At 2345hrs, FOS/Ida informed DM that the family chose to return to the hotel due to long queues at the hospital. Subsequently, the guests returned to the hotel via hotel limousine at 0030hrs on 02Feb. DM met them upon arrival and escorted the family back to Room #2091. DM expressed concern for the child’s condition and noted that swelling persisted. Ice packs, a chocolate box and a hotel teddy bear were provided as gestures of goodwill.

During the conversation, Ms. Zhao expressed that the incident had disrupted their plans and requested hotel compensation. DM acknowledged her concerns and arranged a late check‑out until 1800hrs on 02 Feb. Ms. Zhao additionally requested a complimentary meal for herself and the child, as she needed to remain in the room to observe the child’s condition throughout 02 Feb. As a courtesy, one complimentary IRD breakfast set was arranged. Ms. Zhao thanked for the arrangements and raised no further requests. DM also offered to arrange corner‑guard safety padding in the room to enhance the child’s safety; however, the offer was politely declined by the guest.

-Investigation

•	During the process,  Sonia was unable to locate the guest’s profile in the Opera system,  even after using the lookup function.

After the check in is completed,  the team should escalate the system issue to the Supervisor or Duty Manager,  who will then coordinate with the IT Team for further follow up.

rows.Incident Description:
At approximately 1405hours, the outsource Hong Kong driver, Mr. Mo, reported the Limousine Office regarding a traffic accident involving a Hong Kong–registered Mercedes-Benz Limousine (Car Plate# TH-1682) and a minibus (Car Plate# LK-9848).

The incident occurred on Paterson Street, Causeway Bay, Hong Kong while the Limousine was parked at the roadside after dropping off Ms. Dorothy So. A minibus (Car Plate# LK-9848) collided with the stationary Limousine, resulting in damage to the right front bumper of Limousine.

Driver/ Mr. Mo reported the incident to the Hong Kong Police, and the Hong Kong Traffic Police subsequently issued a case record ticket for the drivers’ reference. In accordance with Hong Kong traffic accident procedures, when an accident does not involve personal injury or serious damage, police officers typically assist the parties in resolving the matter through insurance claims or private settlement. In such cases, officers may only issue a case reference number for record and follow-up purposes.

At the scene, the minibus driver admitted liability and agreed to bear the repair costs. The police facilitated communication by creating a WhatsApp group for both parties and instructed Driver/Mr. Mo to visit an approved Hong Kong repair workshop on the following day to obtain a repair quotation.
rows.Subject: Traffic Accident
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Investigation:
-The Hong Kong traffic accident case reference number: THKI RN 26003714.

Follow Up:
-Mr. Mo will proceed to obtain a repair quotation for Limousine (TH-1682) and will provide an update to Risk Management accordingly.
-Risk Management Team was informed.

In such cases, officers may only issue a case reference number for record and follow-up purposes.

At the scene, the minibus driver admitted liability and agreed to bear the repair costs. The police facilitated communication by creating a WhatsApp group for both parties and instructed Driver/Mr. Mo to visit an approved Hong Kong repair workshop on the following day to obtain a repair quotation.

rows.Incident Description:
At 2141hrs, DM/Karen was informed by FOS/Nico that Mr. Wu, the registrant of due out Room #2292, refused to check out and vacate the room.

Room #2292, C#5034953 was reserved on 03Feb for a one-night stay with scheduled check out on 04Feb. Mr. Wu checked in on 04Feb at 0128hrs. The registration card indicated a check out time of 1200hrs on 04Feb and was signed by the guest. The room remained in due out status on 04Feb. FO conducted departure audits at 1446hrs, 1739hrs, and 1828hrs, during which unpacked luggage was observed in the room. The Tele Marketing team was informed as the guest could not be contacted.

At 2110hrs, Mr. Wu approached FO to retrieve his luggage from the room. FOSA noted the due out status and issued a one-time key access for Bell Services to escort the guest to the room to collect his belongings. At 2125hrs, FOSA conducted a departure audit, during which Mr. Wu stated that he wished to extend the stay and refused to vacate the room. FOSA escalated the matter to FOS. 

FOS attended the room and met with Mr. Wu. FOS advised Mr. Wu to contact his marketing host for a room extension. However, Mr. Wu stated that he would contact the marketing host later after resting. FOS further offered a Hotel Direct Rate for extension, which Mr. Wu declined, insisting again that he would contact marketing for extending the stay after sleeping. The incident was then escalated to DM.

DM attended the room and met with Mr. Wu. DM consulted with Mass ODM and confirmed that the booking could not be extended. FO was advised to proceed with standard procedures and to involve the Security Team if necessary. Security was subsequently summoned for assistance. Upon Security arrival, Mr. Wu claimed that he was feeling dizzy and requested additional time to rest. DM agreed to allow the guest a 30-minute grace period and advised that a departure audit would be conducted at 2230hrs, which the guest acknowledged and accepted.

At 2234hrs, DM returned to the room. Mr. Wu again claimed to be unwell and refused to vacate the room, during which he used foul language. Security contacted the on-site PSP for assistance. PSP arrived, and Mr. Wu collected his luggage and vacated Room #2292, continuing to use foul language. Mr. Wu subsequently left the property. It was confirmed that no property damage was found inside the room. As per Security’s instruction, Mr. Wu has been imposed a one week ban from the property due to non-cooperation and use of foul language.

rows.Incident Description:
At 13:34, Limo Management received host Terry feedback regarding Ms. Yau’s comment that the air-conditioning in vehicle MX9833 felt uncomfortable. She reported that upon entering the vehicle, the cabin felt too warm. After informing the driver, Mr. Ivan Zhou, he immediately adjusted the A/C settings, and Ms. Yau indicated that she felt comfortable afterward. She did not raise any further concerns for the remainder of the trip.

When the vehicle returned from Hong Kong, our Fleet Specialist Peter conducted an immediate inspection. He confirmed that all vehicle functions were operating normally. As per our limousine standard, the A/C is set at 22°C with two bars of airflow. Since our system is a thermostatic air conditioner, when the outside temperature is lower than the preset cabin temperature, the vent air may feel warm.

Following the investigation, we have replied to the host, Mr. Terry, and noted Ms. Yau’s preference. For future arrangements, we will set the vehicle A/C to 19°C with two bars of airflow to better meet her comfort needs.
rows.Subject: Car air Conditioner preference

After issuing new key cards, FOS/Tony attempted to open the door together with the guest; however, both the newly issued keys and the master key also failed to unlock the door. The door lock indicator remained red and the record of Visionline system showing the room door was double locked from inside, although Mr. Yang claimed he was staying alone and didn't use the door lock. The Security Manager was notified immediately for assistance. 

DM and Security Manager proceeded to the 09Floor to meet with Mr. Yang, who was accompanied by FOS. DM apologized to Mr. Yang for the inconvenience caused and learnt from him that the door lock was starting with unstable issue since 2100hrs on 27Feb26. The Security Manager subsequently succeeded in opening the room using the Security master key after DM confirmed that the DM master key also failed to open the door with the indicator light remaining red. Upon entry, the room was confirmed to contain only luggage and no occupants. 

DM offered a room change and arranged fruit amenities to be delivered during the afternoon room make‑up service as a service recovery gesture. The guest accepted and mentioned that he would contact FO for room change after he had rested and woken up. The guest was also informed to contact the Duty Manager if any further assistance was needed. rows.Incident Description:
At 2120hrs, DM/ Chris Chan was notified by the Security Team that Mr. Jiang, the registered guest of Room #1173, had approached the North VIP Registration counter, requesting to file a complaint regarding the handling of a billing-related matter by Security earlier at Gourmet Pavilion.

DM proceeded to the location and met with the guest. According to Mr. Jiang, he had been escorted to the Security Interview Room at 1822hrs on 28 Feb concerning a billing incident at Gourmet Pavilion. He stated that the Security Team had accused him of using another guest’s membership credit to settle a transaction of HKD 1,218.80 on 25 Dec 2025. He was later escorted by Security to Gourmet Pavilion and was requested to settle the outstanding amount.

After paying the amount in cash, Mr. Jiang recalled that he had dined with a friend on that day, and that his friend should have been settled the charges using his friend’s own membership card. He further noted discrepancies with the amount provided by Security—the actual bill should have been HKD 3,984.20, not HKD 1,218.80. Due to these inconsistencies, Mr. Jiang insisted that a mistake had been made and requested a further investigation.

Following a review aligned with the guest’s description, however, due to the expiration of CCTV footage retention, further investigation to verify whether the $1, 218.8 charge was made by Mr. Jiang could not be conducted at this stage. Both the DM and Security SM/ Zhong offered a sincere apology for the inconvenience and distress caused. The previously collected HKD 1,218.80 was returned to Mr. Jiang.

As part of service recovery, the DM offered a fruit platter, room upgrade, and late check-out, all of which Mr. Jiang declined. Instead, he requested an official apology letter from Wynn and HKD 5,000 in cash compensation. The DM respectfully declined the cash compensation request but offered an apology email along with MOP 1,000 in F&B dining credit or one complimentary Spa treatment as an alternative. Mr. Jiang accepted the apology email but maintained his demand for HKD 5,000 cash compensation.

The DM informed Mr. Jiang that his compensation request would be escalated to the Risk Management Team, who would contact him at Tel: +853 6582 8482 at 1500hrs on 02 Mar 2026, per his request. Mr. Jiang accepted this arrangement with no further demands.

rows.Incident Description:
At 1900hrs, DM/Mena was informed by FO RC Team that they received a call from a non-in-house guest Mr. Li (WID#82368028), expressing concern regarding an unauthorized charge of $518 posted to his Wynn Rewards membership account 02Mar2026.

Mr. Li reported that at 1838hrs on 02 March 2026, he received a mobile notification indicating that his membership points had been used to settle a dining bill for Table A83 at Gourmet Pavilion. He clarified that he had not visited Gourmet Pavilion and was not in Macau on the date of the transaction.  Mr. Li further stated that he was concerned his personal information might have been compromised and requested assistance from the hotel.

The Security Team and GP Team were notified immediately. Upon arrival, the Duty Manager and Security Team identified a male and female guest dining at Table A83 and verified that their bill matched the disputed transaction. The female guest, Ms. Feng, admitted that she had purchased the meal at a “35% discount” from an unknown seller on the online platform “Red Note,” paying RMB 336.7. She further stated that the seller subsequently arranged the bill settlement on her behalf.

Following DM and Security's explanation, Ms. Feng expressed her willingness to reimburse the GP dining fee of $518. The amount was subsequently credited back to Mr. Li’s membership account. Ms. Feng has been verbally warned by Security Team regarding the matter.

Mr. Li opted not to escalate the matter to the police and entrusted the Hotel Security Team to further handle the case.  As a precaution, Mr. Liu’s membership account password was reset per Security Team’s recommendation.

rows.Incident Description:
At 1000hrs, DM/Karen was informed by FORC/Macy that Mr. Bogomolny, the registered guest of Room #1926, had called to raise a complaint regarding the Marketing team and his overall experience, and requested to speak with the Duty Manager.

DM/Karen met Mr. Bogomolny in his room to obtain more information. The guest stated that he had booked the room through a Marketing staff member and had the staff’s WhatsApp contact. However, the staff member did not reply to his messages. He added that the Marketing staff had promised to meet and greet him upon arrival and conduct a property tour, but did not show up and never responded to his WhatsApp messages.

He expressed that this experience differed from Wynn Las Vegas and other hotels. The guest mentioned that he had visited Galaxy Hotel with a friend yesterday and noticed a significant difference between Galaxy and Wynn Palace. At Galaxy, Marketing staff conducted property tours and introduced table games to them, whereas at Wynn Palace, no Marketing staff attended to him. The guest hoped to receive a reply from the Marketing team before his departure.

The Duty Manager apologized for the unpleasant experience and assured the guest that his feedback would be relayed to the relevant department heads for improvement. After learning that the guest had not yet consumed breakfast, the DM arranged a Fontana Breakfast for him as a gesture of goodwill and escorted him to Fontana. The guest was advised to contact the Duty Manager if he required any further assistance. Premium Marketing/Gabriela was informed of the incident.

At 1600hrs, the guest approached the North Main Reception for check out. During the confirmation of incidental charges, the guest declined to pay the arrival limousine fee of MOP 2,600, stating that he had not been informed of the charge when the Marketing staff arranged the limousine for him. The DM apologized and advised that the arrival limousine charge would be followed up with the Marketing team. The DM then escorted the guest to the departure limousine.

Before departing, the guest stated that he would further escalate his experience to the Wynn Las Vegas Management Team, as he had still not received any reply from the Marketing team.

rows.Incident Description:
At 0205hrs, DM/Bill was notified by GSC that a non registered female guest, later identified as Ms. Wang, called from room #1798 requesting assistance. She reported that her male companion was experiencing heart discomfort and that she had already contacted ambulance services on her own.

DM/Bill and the Security Team immediately proceeded to Room. Upon arrival, two non registered guests - Ms. Wang and Mr. Fang, were found inside the room. Mr. Fang was conscious, responsive, and able to communicate with the team. It was learned that Mr. Fang has a long term heart condition requiring daily medication. He had taken his medication earlier in the evening but felt unwell during the night.

Shortly after, an ambulance arrived at the South Entrance. Three paramedics attended to the room and assisted Mr. Fang, transporting him to the ambulance via wheelchair. He was taken to CHCSJ Hospital, accompanied by Ms. Wang. Both guests were advised to contact DM upon readiness to return to the hotel for further assistance.

During the incident handling, both Ms. Wang and Mr. Fang were unable to provide the name of the registered guest when questioned. A review of CCTV footage revealed that the registrant, Mr. Liang, had not stayed in the room since his check in on 01 March. Footage also confirmed the room had been occupied by different parties daily, indicating potential room misuse or unauthorized room selling. As a result, Mr. Liang has been placed on the Security Watchlist. Room keys were not overridden at this stage. 

At 0625hrs on 05Mar, both guests returned to room. DM extended a courtesy call to express concern regarding Mr. Fang condition. And confirmed with Ms. Wang that Mr. Fang has obtained medicine from hospital and his condition was getting better. Due to Mr. Fang condition and the late hour, they were allowed to remain in the room until 1100hrs on 05Mar. Room key were overridden asp Security's instruction.

At 1622hrs, DM/Mena was notified by the Security Team of a smoke detector activation in the 2/F Housekeeping Linen Room. DM, Housekeeping, Security, and Facilities teams responded immediately. Upon investigation, the actual activation point was identified as the 2/F Housekeeping Storage Room 1.

No fire, smoke, or property damage was found at the scene. It was determined that the Housekeeping Team had been conducting a training activity during which candles were used to burn and reconnect a broken rope for securing bed linen bags. The smoke generated during this process inadvertently triggered the smoke detector located above them.

The team involved has been coached and reminded not to perform such activities beneath smoke detectors or within enclosed areas where alarms may be activated.

rows.Incident Description:
At 2145hrs, DM/Bill was informed by Bell Captain/Anson that Ms. Huang, the registrant of Room #2324, approached him at the North Main Reception to lodge a complaint regarding the attitude of the Security personnel at the SkyCab Resort Station and concerns about the current SkyCab policy.

According to Ms. Huang, she visited the SkyCab Resort Station with her child at approximately 1800hrs to take the SkyCab. After completing a round trip and returning to the Resort Station, she opted to remain in the cabin to continue toward the Lake Station, as she was planning to proceed to MGM Cotai. A Security staff member then approached her cabin and instructed her to disembark, reportedly using an unfriendly tone.

Ms. Huang explained that she was an in house guest and requested to remain in the cabin, noting that she observed no guests queueing in the priority line. Although the Security personnel eventually stopped insisting that she exit, he proceeded to allow three female guests from the regular line to board her cabin.

Subsequently, when she attempted to return to the hotel via SkyCab at Lake Station at approximately 2100hrs, during which, her child requested to take one more round to enjoy the fountain show as it is his birthday. Ms. Huang reported that she experienced a similar situation during which she was again asked to disembark.

Ms. Huang expressed dissatisfaction with the SkyCab policy, stating that even in house guests appear to be limited to one round trip instead of enjoying multiple or unlimited rides. She stressed that, given the room charges she paid, she expected a clearer sense of guest priority when using the SkyCab.

Bell Captain/Anson apologized to Ms. Huang for the unpleasant experience and offered to summon the Duty Manager for further discussion. Ms. Huang declined, explaining that she was in a hurry to return to her room to arrange dinner for her child.

Following the report, DM/Bill placed a courtesy call to Ms. Huang’s room and extended sincere apologies once again for the incident. DM attempted to offer a form of service recovery like fruit amenities, departure limousine as well as a birthday cake and hotel bear for her child; however, Ms. Huang politely declined all of them and emphasized that her intention in raising the complaint was not to receive compensation. Instead, she wished only to receive the level of consideration and priority she believed she rightfully deserved as a paying in house guest. DM expressed full understanding and assured her that her valuable comments would be conveyed to hotel management for future improvements.
rows.Subject: Guest Complaint - Staff Attitude and Skycab Policy
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Investigation:
-No membership of Ms. Huang - Guest is referral from Executive office.
-No information of the male companion could be obtained,  and it was confirmed via CCTV Footage that who was not at the scene during Ms. Huang's check in process.
  
-According to the CCTV footage,  the following timeline was observed:
18:09:15 – Ms. Huang,  her child,  and a male companion approached the SkyCab Resort Station and boarded Cabin #5.
18:20:48 – Cabin #5 completed one round and returned to the Resort Station. Security Officer #502434 approached the cabin and engaged in a brief conversation. No abnormal motions or inappropriate behavior were observed during the interaction.
At this time,  no guests were queuing in the Priority Line,  and approximately 120 guests were queuing in the Regular Line.
18:21:05 – The Security Officer proceeded to the Regular Line and allowed a party of three female guests to board Ms. Huang’s cabin.
18:25:27 – The cabin arrived at Lake Sation,  Ms. Huang’s party disembarked from the cabin. Ms. Huang and the male companion approached Resort Ambassador/Charlotte to enquire about the SkyCab policy. The guests appeared emotional and were seen pointing toward the Resort Station.
18:27:00 – Ms. Huang and the male companion concluded their conversation with Charlotte and left the area.
21:03:09 – Ms. Huang’s party arrived at the Lake Station and boarded Cabin #20.
21:09:00 – The cabin reached the Resort Station. The guests remained onboard,  and no issues were observed.
21:15:34 – The cabin completed another round and returned to the Lake Station. Security Officer #502440 approached Ms. Huang’s cabin and engaged in a brief conversation. No abnormal behavior was observed.
21:21:45 – The cabin reached the Resort Station again. The guests remained in the cabin without incident.
21:26:56 – The cabin arrived at the Lake Station. No guests were in the Priority Line,  while over 200 guests were queuing in the Regular Line. Security Officer #502440 approached Ms. Huang’s cabin again,  had a short conversation,  and then allowed two female guests from the Regular Line to board.
21:34:00 – The cabin reached the Resort Station. Ms. Huang’s party disembarked. The male companion returned to Room #2324,  while Ms. Huang proceeded to the North Main Reception with her child to raise the complaint with Bell Captain Anson.

Follow Up:
-VIP/Arie was notified.
-EO/Charlotte was notified.
-BDV/Ben was notified.
-Security OM/Locke was notified.
-DM please arrange to see off the guest with a chocolate gift box as a gesture of hotel goodwill and courtesy.

As a gesture of goodwill,  DM offered a late check-out at 16:00hrs and departure limousine service,  both of which the guest accepted. Luggage-down assistance was also offered; however,  the guest declined. Ms. Huang thanked for the follow-up and did not pursue the matter further.

rows.Incident Description:
At 1828hrs, DM/Mena was notified by GSC Team that a female guest from Room #2382 and reported her child had accidentally bumped his face and sustained an injury, requesting first aid assistance.

DM and Security Team responded to the room, met the registrant, Mr. Chen, his wife Ms. Fan, and their two children (a 6‑year‑old girl and an injured 5‑year‑old boy).

Upon assessment, the 5‑year‑old boy was observed to have mild redness and superficial abrasions of approximately 1 cm on the right cheekbone area. No active bleeding was noted. According to the mother, the injury occurred while the child was playing in the living room near the tea table and accidentally struck the corner of the table. She indicated her intention to apply medicated oil to the affected area.

The parents declined further medical evaluation at a hospital. They also declined the installation of corner guards and a bed rail for additional in-room safety. At 2314hrs, DM/Chris Lee was informed by GSC that the registered guest of Room #1558, Mr. He, reported a power outage in the room.

rows.Incident Description:
At 0035hrs on 10 Mar, DM Chris Lee was notified by GSC that the registered guest of Room #2081, Mr. Chen, reported his jade ring missing and requested assistance. DM and the Security Team responded to the room and conducted a thorough search; however, the ring could not be located.

During enquiry, Mr. Chen stated that he had placed the ring on the bedside table before leaving the room in the morning. He confirmed that he stayed alone, though two female friends visited his room on 09 Mar. Mr. Chen advised that he had checked with both individuals, and they assured him they did not touch the ring.

-Following a review of CCTV footage, the following was established:
09 Mar 2026
•	0031hrs: Mr. Chen was seen wearing the jade ring on his right-hand ring finger when entering Room #2081 with two female friends.
•	0036hrs: The two female exited the room and returned to Room #1332. 
•	Although Mr. Chen declined to disclose their details, one individual was identified via CCTV as Ms. Chen (WID8164393 – Red Card), the registrant of Room #1332.
•	1107hrs: Mr. Chen exited Room #2081; CCTV confirmed he was not wearing the ring at that time.
•	1954hrs: Mr. Chen returned to the room #2081 with the two females; CCTV confirmed he was not wearing the ring at that time.
•	2015hrs: Mr. Chen exited Room #2081 with the two females; CCTV confirmed he was not wearing the ring at that time.
•	2353hrs: Mr. Chen returned to the room #2081 with the two females; CCTV confirmed he was not wearing the ring at that time. 
•	2358hrs: The two female exited the room and returned to Room #1332. 

Based on the findings, Mr. Chen elected to seek police assistance. PSP officers were called to the scene to manage the situation. Following an initial investigation, the case was transferred to PJ for further handling. At 0500hrs, Mr. Chen was escorted to the PJ headquarters for continued investigation. A DM business card was provided to him for contact upon completion of the procedures.

At 0720hrs, Mr. Chen contacted the DM requesting transportation back to the hotel. A hotel limousine was arranged accordingly. Mr. Chen expressed his appreciation for the assistance and had no further requests.

rows.Incident Description:
At 07:51, dispatcher Kiko notified Teams group that VIP service had just delivered LC coffee at 07:49, and limo was rushing to LC home. Means that a potentially limo service delay occurred.

At 08:03, LC called dispatch office to ask for the limo location. Dispatcher Sam informed that limo was near pick up location and get ready to turn in, as the coffee had been delivered late.

At 08:05, limo arrived at LC home, and LC boarded the limo at 08:08. LC arrived at destination at 08:18.

At 08:12, Charlotte called dispatch office to ask why the limo was late. Dispatcher Sam replied that the delay was due to the coffee being delivered to the limo late. Charlotte said she would follow up with VIP service for more information.
rows.Subject: Delay Pick Up or Drop Off - WMP
rows.Investigation/Follow Up 1: Delay Pick Up or Drop Off - WMP
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Investigation:

At 07:18,  driver Chio In left WP car park and went to MUST to make sure drop-off location,  then returned to stand by at WPN at 07:25.  
At 07:42,  dispatcher Kiko called VIP Service for a follow-up on the coffee delivery.  
At 07:47,  dispatcher Kiko made the second follow-up to VIP Service regarding the coffee delivery.  
At 07:49,  VIP Service delivered the coffee to limo,  and limo left WPN at 07:50.  
At 08:03,  LC called Dispatch and asked for the limo location.  
At 08:04,  limo arrived at LC’s home and boarded limo at 08:08.  
At 08:09,  dispatch informed booker Sandy that LC had been picked up.  
At 08:18,  limo arrived at MUST.

Follow up:

At 08:14,  limo informed VIP service team there was 5 mins limo service delayed for LC picked up.  VIP service AVP Ms. Yeung informed that VIP service team has explained to Charlotte regarding limo service was caused by VIP Service and case was settled.

Briefing all dispatcher to ensure limo updates booker immediately if there is any potential service delay (e.g. traffic,  waiting time,  accident)

rows.Incident Description:
At 1825hrs, DM was informed by FOS/Johnny of a guest key malfunction incident involving Mr. Feng, the registrant of Room #2520. Details as below:

•	1800hrs: Mr. Feng completed check in for Room #2520.
•	1818hrs: Mr. Feng returned to Reception and reported that the guestroom key cards were not functioning and he was unable to access the room. As Mr. Feng declined a room change and preferred to remain in the same room, FOS reissued new key cards and accompanied the guests back to the room for assistance.
•	Upon testing, both the newly issued Opera and Visionline guest key cards failed to unlock the door. The door lock indicator displayed a red light, and Visionline system records indicated that the guest card access had been overridden with an error.
•	The staff master key was used successfully to unlock the door, allowing the guests to enter the room.
•	Sincere apologies were extended to Mr. Feng for the inconvenience caused. He was informed that the issue would be escalated immediately to Management and the relevant department for prompt rectification. Mr. Feng acknowledged the explanation, placed his belongings in the room, and subsequently proceeded to the Casino area.

Following the report, DM contacted the Access Control Team, and repair works were completed at 1940hrs. Based on preliminary assessment, the malfunction was attributed to a system error. The electronic circuit board of the door lock was replaced, followed by multiple key‑testing cycles, after which the lock resumed normal operation. The door lock batteries were also replaced.

DM attempted to contact Mr. Feng to follow up on reissuance of new room keys; however, the contact attempt was unsuccessful. The guest’s host, Celia, was subsequently informed and assisted in advising the guest to contact DM for key reissuance prior to returning to the room.

At 2235hrs, Mr. Feng approached North VIP Registration, DM met with the guest to extend sincere apologies once again for the inconvenience caused. The guest accepted the apology without further pursuit and politely declined the fruit and sweet amenities offered by DM. He was advised to contact DM should any further assistance be required and was escorted to the lift lobby thereafter.

Investigation:
-Membership tier of the registrant - Mr. Feng: Chairman Card.

•	The guest checked in at 1800hrs.

-DM please take note.

rows.Incident Description:
At 1957hrs, DM/Mena was notified by GSC Team that a male guest from Room #0547 requested to speak with the Manager on Duty to raise a privacy-related concern. The guest reported that a staff was allegedly seen standing on the external platform outside the room window and looking into the guest room.

DM attended the room and met with the registrant, Mr. Zhao, along with two non-registered guests, Mr. Zhang and Mr. Huang. According to the guests, at approximately 1920hrs, only Mr. Zhang and his girlfriend were inside the room and resting on the bed without dressing. They reported observing a person on the exterior platform outside the window who appeared to look into the room. Mr. Zhang stated that the individual squatted down and left the area after making eye contact with them.

Mr. Zhang expressed concern that the individual might have recorded footage of them, resulting in a potential privacy breach. He requested the hotel’s assistance in reviewing CCTV footage to identify the individual and to confirm whether any recording had taken place. The Security Team was informed accordingly to support the CCTV review.

DM extended sincere apologies to the guests for the unexpected experience and acknowledged their concerns. The guests were assured that an investigation would be conducted and that updates would be provided as soon as available. The guests accepted the explanation and declined the room charge offered by DM. 

Following the meeting, DM and the Security Team inspected the external roof platform, which is accessible via Staircases #1 (North side) and #7 (South side). No individuals were found on the platform at the time of inspection. It was confirmed that there is no CCTV coverage on the platform itself, except at the access points of Staircases #1 and #7.

Based on the CCTV footage review between 1852hrs and 2004hrs, two male workers from an outsourced vendor were observed entering and exiting the roof platform area via the 5/F Staircase #1. No personnel were recorded accessing the platform via Staircase #7 during the same period.

The guests were subsequently briefed on the investigation findings at the current stage. Thereafter, the guest elected to report the matter to the Police independently. PSP officers arrived on scene and conducted interviews with the guests. Mr. Zhang subsequently accompanied the officers to Police Headquarters for further investigation.

CCTV Footage confirmed Mr. Zhang returned to the hotel by Taxi at 2319hrs and went to the casino.

rows.Incident Description:
At 1800hrs, DM/Bill was notified by the Security Team that the staff of 99 Noodles had reported damage to tableware, specifically one spoon and one teacup, caused by a disorderly guest. Security assistance was requested.

According to 99 Noodles, at approximately 1730hrs, a female guest—later identified as Ms. Miao, the registrant of Room #979—raised a complaint regarding a service oversight while food orders were being taken. During the interaction, Ms. Miao became agitated and forcefully slammed a spoon and teacup onto the table, resulting in damage to both items. Ms. Miao subsequently left the venue. CCTV footage later confirmed that she returned to Room #979 following the incident.

DM/Bill and Security SM/Ego attended Room #979 and met Ms. Miao. During the enquiry, Ms. Miao apologized for her behavior and advised that she suffers from diabetes and a depressive disorder. She explained that the incident stemmed from an incorrect food order provided by 99 Noodles on the night of 29 March, with details as follows:
•	At 2320hrs on 29 Mar, Ms. Miao ordered Shanxi noodles for dine in and a takeaway order of Wok Fried Prawn with Cashew Nuts and Dried Chili.
•	After returning to her room, she consumed only the Shanxi noodles and did not open the takeaway box. She then returned to the casino and gambled until approximately 0650hrs on 30 Mar.
•	Upon opening the takeaway box, she discovered that the item provided was Wok Fried Crispy Prawn with Sweet and Sour Sauce instead of her original order. As the dish was too sweet for her due to her diabetic condition, she did not consume it and went to sleep.
•	At 1728hrs on 30 Mar, Ms. Miao returned to 99 Noodles with the takeaway item and requested an exchange. The request was declined by staff due to the time elapsed since purchase. Ms. Miao stated that she became increasingly upset and lost control as she was hungry and emotionally distressed.
•	Ms. Miao reiterated her apologies and confirmed her willingness to compensate for the damaged items.

Following further discussion, DM and Security issued Ms. Miao a verbal warning and advised that ban action would be imposed should any similar incident reoccur. Ms. Miao acknowledged and accepted the warning.

Confirmation with 99 Noodles/Amanda indicated that the total damage charge amounted to MOP 66. As a gesture of goodwill and hotel courtesy, the charge was waived by DM.

A further investigation was conducted with 99 Noodles/Alice, along with a review of CCTV footage. During the incident, shards from the damaged teacup flew toward two female patrons seated at a nearby table, prompting one of them to stand up to avoid potential injury. The affected guests were promptly escorted to another table, and new dishes were provided to prevent food contamination from fragments. No injuries were reported by the guests.
rows.Subject: Security Assistance - Disorderly Conduct
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Investigation:
-Membership Tier of Ms. Miao: Gold Card.
-CCTV coverage was insufficient to positively identify the two affected female patrons.

-Confirmation with 99 Noodles (Alice):
•	Ms. Miao is a repeat guest and customarily places her orders without referring to the menu.
•	During her visit on 29 Mar,  she verbally requested “Fried Prawn, ” consistent with her usual ordering practice.
•	Based on this request,  the server proceeded to place an order for Wok Fried Crispy Prawn with Sweet and Sour Sauce.
•	The Wok Fried Crispy Prawn with Sweet and Sour Sauce is part of the seasonal specialties menu,  with supply scheduled to end on 01 Apr 2026.
•	The ingredient composition of Wok Fried Prawn with Cashew Nuts and Dried Chili and Wok Fried Crispy Prawn with Sweet and Sour Sauce is largely identical,  with the exception of the addition of dried chili and cashew nuts in the former. As such,  the sugar level in both dishes is nearly the same.

Follow Up:

-DM please take note.
